capcom's first release: mission control for your Claude Code spend. It reads the logs Claude Code keeps on your machine and shows where your tokens and dollars go, why the spend jumped, and which habits of your setup cost the most, with the change to make.

![capcom's website in six steps: spend jumped, why, where, which step, is it a habit, did it work](https://github.com/brenocq/capcom/raw/assets/demo-light.webp)

## Install

```
uv tool install capcom
capcom scan
capcom serve --open
```

You need Python 3.12 or newer. It uses only the standard library.

## What's in it

- **Spend, adding up:** two weeks of spend by project, model, agent type or day, with numbered spike markers. Any day opens into its 24 hours.
- **Why it jumped:** each spike comes with its cause and the dollars it added, for example a cache that expired 12 times while Bash ran.
- **Every session on one timeline:** context and spend rate per request, with subagents in their own lanes. Long pauses are squeezed, and you can zoom in.
- **Every step of an agent:** an agent's page from spawn to hand-back, showing what it ran, how long each step took and what it cost. In `capcom serve` you can open any step to read the call and its output, live from the log and never stored. Unnamed phases get names from the calls' own descriptions.
- **Checks:** setup habits ranked by what they would save a week, with the change to make. `capcom mark` and Did it work? then compare the weeks before and after.
- **Limits:** the 5-hour and weekly windows, where they stand now and where they will be at the reset. Turn it on once with `capcom limits --install`.
- **Ask Roger:** an opt-in chat that asks your own `claude` CLI (Haiku) about what you're looking at. It sends only capcom's numbers and labels, never your prompts, file contents or tool output. `--no-ask` turns it off.
- **Private:** your logs are read read-only, there are no network requests except Ask Roger, and the website listens on 127.0.0.1 only.

It also reads OpenClaw's logs.

capcom is new and may still get things wrong. Its dollars are API-equivalent estimates, not your bill. Please [open an issue](https://github.com/brenocq/capcom/issues) when something looks off.
